react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis tools (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) independently converged on KEGG:hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as the dominant affected pathway, with FDR as low as 9.58e-15 (RaMP) and p = 1.59e-08 (MetaboAnalystR). Six of the ten input metabolites map to this pathway: L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), and tryptamine (C00398). These cover both the serotonin/melatonin biosynthetic arm and the kynurenine/3-hydroxyanthranilic acid catabolic arm of tryptophan catabolism. Reactome REACT:R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) appeared as a sub-pathway hit at FDR 6.64e-08, implicating the terminal biosynthetic module specifically. WikiPathways WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism) ranked #2 in RaMP (FDR 1.14e-14), confirming the signal across databases. The non-tryptophan metabolites doxycycline, acrolein, milrinone, and a mismapped cytidine-2',3'-cyclic-phosphate (KEGG:C00127 resolves to glutathione disulfide, not the user-supplied name) did not contribute to enriched pathways. Mummichog returned no hits (human_mfn reference lacks these metabolites), and FELLA RWR errored at runtime, leaving ORA as the sole paradigm. Cross-paradigm consensus on tryptophan metabolism is strong, with six driver metabolites and consistent fold-enrichment >500 across methods.
